summary: Tested both new enhancements. BACKEND (/api/analytics + reschedule): 3/3 pytest cases pass — response contains all required keys (published_total, scheduled_total, failed_total, by_platform, by_type, by_hour with 24 keys, dlq list, feedback list); unauthorized returns 401; POST /api/atoms/<id>/schedule with a new date moves the atom into a new day bucket while preserving time-of-day. FRONTEND: Sidebar nav-analytics → /analytics renders 'Analitik & Geri Besleme' with 3 stat cards (Yayınlanan=1, Zamanlanmış=2, Başarısız=0) and all required data-testids: bars-platform, bars-type, bars-hour, feedback-list, dlq-list. DLQ empty → shows 'Başarısız yayın yok 🎉' (no dlq-retry- buttons — correct per spec). /schedule shows 14/14 day-<i> zones and 2 draggable Twitter/X timeline-<id> cards. DRAG-DROP verified via native Playwright drag_to: card moved from day-0 → day-3, ended up under the new day zone, success toast 'Yeniden zamanlandı' shown. No console errors on either page.
critical_code_review_comments: Analytics.jsx retry() sets scheduled_at=new Date().toISOString() (immediate). Fine for DLQ retry but stacks work in the next 1-min publisher tick — acceptable.

Schedule.jsx dropOnDay uses new Date(day).setHours(orig.getHours(), orig.getMinutes(),...) then toISOString. This uses local timezone of the browser; since the day-<i> zones are created via new Date() with local midnight, the produced ISO correctly maps back to the same displayed day after reload.
Backend /api/analytics: dlq entries omit article_title/content — UI only shows platform+label which is enough, but including article_title would improve DLQ operator context.

server.py analytics(): parses published_at via fromisoformat; if a legacy record stores non-ISO string it is silently skipped (try/except pass). Acceptable but a debug log would help diagnose gaps in by_hour.
seed_data_creation: None. Used existing 2 pending Twitter/X scheduled atoms. Backend reschedule test restores original scheduled_at. Frontend drag-drop test moved one atom from day-0 to day-3 and left it there (per instructions cleanup is not required; publisher will attempt at that future time and hit expected Twitter 402).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Analytics + drag-drop reschedule both fully working. Playwright native drag_to() WORKS with the HTML5 draggable/onDrop implementation in Schedule.jsx — no need to fall back to raw API. auto-distribute-btn is only rendered when unscheduled.length>0 (per code); during this run unscheduled=0 so it was absent — not a bug. published- anchor didn't render because the only published atom lacked scheduled_at in timeline; not a regression per iteration_4 note.
